scope: General education and unreleased planning candidates only; source verification is not medical review or release approval.
predicate_contract: applicability.all contains {flag, equals:boolean}; evaluate against facts.flags using strict boolean equality. Missing flags never match. An empty all means general education, not a diagnosis or individual prescription.
question_ids_role: Question IDs are relevance anchors to the canonical questionnaire, not evidence of diagnosis, mechanism, age, or treatment eligibility.

sources.title: Behavioral and psychological treatments for chronic insomnia disorder in adults: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline
sources.verification_excerpt: Recommendation 1 assigns multicomponent CBT-I STRONG; recommendations 3 and 5 assign stimulus control and relaxation CONDITIONAL; recommendation 6 advises against sleep hygiene alone.
sources.support_location: PubMed title/authors/DOI and abstract Recommendations 1, 3, 5, 6; AASM announcement treatment and diagnostic-context paragraphs (published December 2020 for the February 2021 guideline).
sources.verification_method: Browser read of PubMed abstract and fetch of AASM announcement; excerpt is a verification summary, not a verbatim quotation.

sources.title: Recommended Amount of Sleep for a Healthy Adult: A Joint Consensus Statement of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine and Sleep Research Society
sources.organization: American Academy of Sleep Medicine and Sleep Research Society
sources.verification_excerpt: AASM/SRS recommend seven or more hours; the panel addressed adults aged 18 to 60. Timing, daily regularity, quality and absence of sleep disorders also matter. More than nine hours may be appropriate in specified circumstances.
sources.support_location: PubMed bibliographic record confirms JCSM version and DOI; AASM June 1, 2015 announcement paragraphs on recommendation, no upper limit, multidimensional sleep, and panel population. The announcement links the parallel SLEEP publication, not the JCSM DOI.
sources.verification_method: Browser read of PubMed metadata/abstract plus fetch of the authoritative society announcement for exact recommendation and population; summary, not verbatim quotation.

sources.title: The effects of bedtime writing on difficulty falling asleep: A polysomnographic study comparing to-do lists and completed activity lists
sources.verification_excerpt: Fifty-seven healthy adults aged 18–30 were randomized to five minutes of future-task or completed-task writing before overnight polysomnography. The to-do group fell asleep faster than the completed-list group; specificity was associated with latency within the to-do condition.
sources.support_location: PubMed abstract, methods and results; bibliographic header records January 2018 issue and October 2017 electronic publication.
sources.verification_method: Browser read of PubMed title/authors/DOI and abstract; summary, not verbatim quotation. No blocked PMC content was used as verified support.

sources.title: The two-process model of sleep regulation: a reappraisal
sources.verification_excerpt: The model posits interaction of homeostatic Process S and circadian-pacemaker-controlled Process C and is a conceptual framework for sleep regulation.
sources.support_location: PubMed abstract, opening model description and conclusion; title/authors/DOI header.
sources.verification_method: Browser read of PubMed abstract and bibliographic metadata; summary, not verbatim quotation; no inference of an individual's physiology.

sources.title: The consensus sleep diary: standardizing prospective sleep self-monitoring
sources.verification_excerpt: The Core diary has nine items covering bed/attempted sleep times, latency, number/duration of awakenings, final awakening/rise time, perceived quality and comments; morning completion within one hour of rising. The proposed diary still needed testing, refinement and validation.
sources.support_location: Full text: The Core Consensus Sleep Diary (under development/results); abstract Conclusions. PubMed confirms authors, publication date and DOI.
sources.verification_method: Browser read of PubMed and PMC full text after normal site challenge completed; summary, not verbatim quotation.

sources.title: Sleep Deprivation and Deficiency: Healthy Sleep Habits
sources.organization: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute, National Institutes of Health
sources.verification_excerpt: Give yourself enough time to sleep; go to bed and wake at the same time each day; use the hour before bed for quiet time; relaxation techniques before bed may help. Shift workers receive separate advice.
sources.support_location: Opening adequate-sleep paragraph, sleep-habits bullet list, Strategies for shift workers; page last updated March 24, 2022.
sources.verification_method: Fetched actual NHLBI educational page; summary, not verbatim quotation. Update year is not a trial publication year.

claims.approved_claim: The AASM 2021 guideline strongly recommends that clinicians use multicomponent CBT-I for chronic insomnia disorder in adults.
claims.plain_serbian: Za hroničnu nesanicu kod odraslih, smernice snažno preporučuju višekomponentnu kognitivno-bihejvioralnu terapiju za nesanicu uz stručnu procenu. Ovaj upitnik ne utvrđuje da li imaš taj poremećaj.
exclusions: Do not diagnose chronic insomnia from questionnaire flags.
Do not present this product as CBT-I.
claims.directness: Direct for adult chronic-insomnia clinical treatment; educational only here.
limitations: Recommendation strength is not a personalized success probability.
Duration, frequency, adequate sleep opportunity and differential diagnosis are not established by the questionnaire.

claims.approved_claim: AASM conditionally suggests clinician use of stimulus control as a single-component therapy for adult chronic insomnia disorder.
claims.plain_serbian: Kontrola stimulusa je jedna od terapijskih mogućnosti za hroničnu nesanicu kod odraslih. Preporuka je uslovna i zahteva stručni izbor; ovde nije uputstvo za samostalno lečenje.
exclusions: No autonomous stimulus-control protocol.
No mandatory leaving-bed timers or fixed wake prescriptions.
claims.directness: Direct clinical recommendation; not direct support for unsupervised product actions.
limitations: Clinical assessment and patient preferences matter.
Mobility and safety are not assessed.

reviewmetadata.support_location: Abstract Recommendation 3 and definition of conditional

claims.approved_claim: AASM conditionally suggests clinician use of relaxation therapy as a single-component treatment for adult chronic insomnia disorder.
claims.plain_serbian: Terapija relaksacijom ima uslovnu preporuku za hroničnu nesanicu kod odraslih. To ne znači da bilo koja kratka vežba sigurno poboljšava san, niti da je takva terapija potrebna baš tebi.
exclusions: No clinical relaxation protocol without assessment.
No prescribed breathing rates, breath holds or muscle-tension regimen.
does_not_establish: Benefit of a specific breathing exercise
claims.directness: Direct for clinical relaxation therapy, not a generic exercise dose.
limitations: Cannot transfer clinical-treatment findings to an unspecified wellness exercise.
Relevant clinical history is unknown.

claims.approved_claim: AASM conditionally recommends against sleep hygiene as the sole treatment for adult chronic insomnia disorder.
claims.plain_serbian: Opšte navike pred spavanje nisu dovoljne kao samostalno lečenje hronične nesanice. Ako teškoće traju ili ometaju dan, same promene rutine ne treba da zamene stručnu procenu.
exclusions: Do not claim that habits are useless.
Do not substitute a routine for clinical care.
claims.directness: Direct for standalone treatment of adult chronic insomnia.
limitations: Does not prohibit general educational sleep-habit advice.

claims.approved_claim: The AASM/SRS consensus addressing healthy adults aged 18–60 recommends regularly obtaining at least seven hours of sleep per night.
claims.plain_serbian: Za zdrave odrasle od 18 do 60 godina, opšta preporuka je najmanje sedam sati sna tokom noći redovno. To nije lični recept: tvoje godine, zdravlje i tačne potrebe nisu utvrđeni ovim upitnikom.
exclusions: Do not apply as a pediatric or older-adult prescription.
Do not infer age or exact duration from a broad answer range.
does_not_establish: That seven hours is sufficient for everyone
An upper limit of nine hours
That fatigue is caused by insufficient sleep
claims.directness: Direct population guidance; no individualized age inference. Missing age does not block population-limited education.
limitations: Consensus scope 18–60 years.
Questionnaire does not measure sleep objectively.

reviewmetadata.support_location: AASM announcement recommendation and panel-population paragraphs; PubMed DOI metadata

claims.approved_claim: AASM/SRS describe healthy sleep as requiring adequate duration, appropriate timing, daily regularity, good quality and absence of sleep disorders.
claims.plain_serbian: Trajanje nije jedini deo zdravog sna: važni su i vreme spavanja, redovnost, kvalitet i odsustvo poremećaja sna. Broj sati sam ne objašnjava kako se osećaš ujutru.
exclusions: Do not claim a questionnaire measures circadian phase or rules out disorders.
claims.directness: Direct general description; individual connections remain observational.
limitations: No causal attribution to a particular answer.
Perceived quality is not a clinical assessment.

reviewmetadata.support_location: AASM announcement paragraph beginning The benefits of healthy sleep

claims.approved_claim: The consensus does not set a universal upper limit; more than nine hours may be appropriate for young adults, recovery from sleep debt, or illness.
claims.plain_serbian: Više od devet sati sna nije samo po sebi dokaz problema: nekim mladim odraslima, pri nadoknadi manjka sna ili tokom bolesti može odgovarati duži san. Ovaj odgovor ne otkriva razlog dužeg spavanja.
exclusions: Do not label long sleep inherently harmful.
Do not equate sleeping longer without an alarm with sleep debt.
does_not_establish: That persistent unrefreshing sleep needs no assessment
claims.directness: Direct exception/context statement, not a long-sleep diagnosis.
limitations: Health and sleep-debt history are unknown.

reviewmetadata.support_location: AASM announcement no-upper-limit and more-than-nine-hours paragraphs

claims.approved_claim: In one randomized laboratory night with 57 healthy adults aged 18–30, five minutes of to-do-list writing before sleep produced faster sleep onset than writing about completed activities.
claims.plain_serbian: U maloj laboratorijskoj studiji sa 57 zdravih osoba od 18 do 30 godina, pet minuta pisanja budućih obaveza bilo je povezano sa bržim uspavljivanjem nego pisanje završenih aktivnosti. To nije dokaz da će pisanje pomoći tebi ili lečiti nesanicu.
exclusions: Stop an optional writing experiment if it increases distress or rumination.
Do not substitute for assessment of persistent symptoms.
does_not_establish: Effect in clinical insomnia or all ages
Earlier-evening writing has the same effect
claims.directness: Direct for the studied comparison and population; indirect for an optional home experiment.
limitations: 57 participants aged 18–30.
One controlled laboratory night.
Completed-activity-list comparator, not a no-writing control.
Active thoughts do not identify the studied mechanism.

reviewmetadata.support_location: PubMed abstract randomized writing conditions and result

claims.approved_claim: Within the study's to-do-list condition, more specific lists were associated with shorter subsequent sleep-onset latency; specificity was not separately randomized.
claims.plain_serbian: U istoj maloj studiji, konkretnije liste budućih obaveza bile su povezane sa kraćim uspavljivanjem. To je povezanost unutar grupe, a ne dokaz da dodavanje detalja uzrokuje bolji san.
exclusions: Do not encourage prolonged or exhaustive planning.
limitations: Not independent replication of TODO_WRITING_LAB.
Specificity was not randomized.
Same small young-adult one-night sample.

claims.approved_claim: The two-process model describes sleep regulation through interacting homeostatic and circadian processes; it is a conceptual framework, not an individual assessment.
claims.plain_serbian: Jedan važan model opisuje san kroz međudelovanje potrebe za snom i dnevnog biološkog ritma. Odgovori na ovaj upitnik ne mere te procese i ne pokazuju da je tvoj ritam poremećen.
exclusions: No inferred circadian-phase defect.
No prescribed sleep deprivation or light dose.
claims.directness: Direct model description; no individual mechanistic inference.
limitations: Not a trial of wake-regularity actions.
Questionnaire does not measure homeostatic or circadian physiology.

reviewmetadata.support_location: PubMed abstract Process S and Process C description

claims.approved_claim: The Consensus Sleep Diary separately records sleep timing, onset latency, awakenings, perceived quality and comments, with Core entries completed in the morning within one hour of rising.
claims.plain_serbian: Dnevnik sna odvojeno beleži vreme spavanja, uspavljivanje, buđenja i lični utisak o kvalitetu. Kratak jutarnji zapis može služiti posmatranju; nije dijagnoza niti dokaz da će praćenje popraviti san.
exclusions: No overnight alarms or clock-checking for measurement.
Stop optional tracking if it increases preoccupation.
does_not_establish: That this abbreviated log is the validated Consensus Sleep Diary
claims.directness: Direct for diary structure; abbreviated product observations are an adaptation, not the published instrument.
limitations: Subjective self-report.
No efficacy trial of tracking in this paper.
Do not reproduce the published diary or claim instrument equivalence.

reviewmetadata.support_location: PMC full text The Core Consensus Sleep Diary

claims.approved_claim: The 2012 diary-development paper explicitly states that its proposed diary still required testing, refinement and validation; it does not validate this questionnaire or an abbreviated product log.
claims.plain_serbian: Rad iz 2012. predstavlja razvoj standardizovanog dnevnika i tada navodi potrebu za daljim proverama. On ne potvrđuje validnost ovog upitnika niti skraćenih beleški u ovom proizvodu.
exclusions: Do not claim the diary has never subsequently been validated.
Do not use this paper as validation of product scores.
does_not_establish: Current validation status of the original diary
claims.directness: Direct statement about this 2012 publication only.
limitations: Later diary-validation studies were not assessed in this registry.

claims.approved_claim: NHLBI advises using the hour before bed for quiet time as general sleep-habit guidance; this is not a trial proving a particular wind-down routine treats insomnia.
claims.plain_serbian: NHLBI savetuje mirniji period pred spavanje kao opštu naviku. Kratka pauza od sadržaja može biti dobrovoljan pokušaj, bez obećanja da će ubrzati uspavljivanje ili lečiti nesanicu.
exclusions: No claim that screens caused this person's difficulty.
No precise light dosing or rigid routine duration.
does_not_establish: Trial efficacy of a short content break
A causal effect of this person's screen use
claims.directness: Direct guidance; a short optional pause is a pragmatic adaptation with unestablished efficacy.
limitations: No trial effect size or guarantee.
Not standalone chronic-insomnia treatment.

claims.approved_claim: NHLBI advises regular bed and wake times while allowing enough time for sleep; shift workers have separate guidance. This does not establish a personalized fixed wake time.
claims.plain_serbian: Opšti savet je sličnije vreme spavanja i ustajanja, uz dovoljno vremena za san. Raspored treba prilagoditi obavezama; ne skraćuj san da bi pratio/la satnicu, a smenski rad zahteva poseban pristup.
exclusions: No wake-time prescription that reduces sleep opportunity.
Do not assume a non-shift-work schedule.
does_not_establish: That an alarm difficulty indicates circadian dysfunction
claims.directness: Direct public-health advice; individual scheduling requires feasibility and adequate sleep opportunity.
limitations: Age and work schedule are not inferred.
No efficacy trial of this product's scheduling experiment.

reviewmetadata.support_location: NHLBI opening adequate-time paragraph, regular-times bullets and shift-work section
